The Western Mockhound Association hopreciates the opportunity of commenting upon the subject draft statement. our membership, now in 27 states, is predominently outdoorsmen. We address our remarks in behalf of the quarter million rock hounds who regularly visit outdoor sites on public land in the western United States.
The rockhound may not be the target for which Executive Order was written; but unless hobbiests have access to remote areas by use of primitive unmaintained roads that they have been using for decades, rockhounding will be unable to survive.
The subject Executive Order 11644 and statement clearly have been written to cover eyelists; four-wheelers and dune buggies, but in the process it gravely affects rockhounds as well as every other outdoorsman...campers, hunters, fishermen, and any one who uses a vehicle for access to areas away from paved roads. We want to stress the fact that there is a fundamental difference between the rockhound on the one hand, and the cyclist, four-wheeler and dune buggiest on the other hand. It is a matter of vehicle use. The latter group use their vehicle for the pleasure of the ride, whereas rockhounds use theirs as a means of transportation over rou harcads to a sociite collecting area or in search of one.
